transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-04-09 15:00 PDT | Duration: 58m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Clara Nguyen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood Product), Liam O'Connor (NovaRetail ML Eng), Priya Rao (NovaRetail Platform), Darren Holt (CTO), Maya (Data Scientist)

[00:00] Clara: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're gonna walk through Redwood Optimize and specifically how our quantization profiles for INT8 and FP8 behave — latency, cost, and quality tradeoffs. Samir will run the live console demo. Quick intro round?
[00:18] Liam: Liam here, ML eng; focused on inference cost. We run a recommendation reranker and are curious about tail latency.
[00:26] Priya: Priya, infra/platform. We care about VPC, KMS, and can we run private?
[00:32] Darren: Darren, CTO. Timeline: pilot in 2–3 weeks ideally.
[00:36] Clara: Great. Samir, jump in.
[00:40] Samir: Cool. I'm gonna share my screen — give me a sec. (screen share) Okay, Optimize console: top-right you see Profiles -> Quantization. We ship sample profiles: INT8-aggressive, INT8-conservative, FP8-balanced. These encode kernel choices, per-layer scaling.
[01:10] Maya: When you say FP8-balanced, is that the new bfloat-ish 8-bit or a custom FP8?
[01:15] Samir: Good call. It's a vendor-agnostic FP8 emulation that maps to reduced-precision kernels; on NVIDIA we map to TensorFloat-friendly kernels. Transcription note: sometimes tools transcribe it as F P eight or F P ate.
[01:30] Liam: Walk me through the expected quality delta. Like, what's the hit on our ranker MAP?
[01:35] Samir: From our benchmark set, INT8-aggressive reduced model size and improved latency ~30–45% at token gen, but MAP dropped ~4–8% on open-domain prompts. FP8-balanced tends to give 15–25% latency improvement with MAP drop of 1–3% on typical ranking tasks. But that varies by layer sensitivity.
[02:05] Priya: Are those numbers from the hosted infra or dedicated? We need to know since our infra is on GCP with T4s for dev and A100s in prod.
[02:15] Samir: Good point. Benchmarks were run on A100-80gb reserved nodes. On T4 you'd see different kernel throughput and less FP8 efficiency; INT8 often performs relatively better on T4s. We'll attach the spreadsheet.
[02:28] Darren: Can we do mixed profiles? Some routes INT8, some FP8? Our storefront needs top-k re-rank to be high fidelity but category-level responses can be lower fidelity.
[02:37] Jordan: Yes — Optimize supports per-route quantization policies. You can pin a per-route profile via the Console or API. We also show projected cost and latency delta per route.
[02:50] Liam: How do you measure quality in Optimize? Is it automatic or do we upload evals?
[02:55] Samir: You upload an eval set — Optimize will run reg tests across candidate quant profiles, compute your chosen metrics (exact-match, ROUGE, MAP, MRR). It also surfaces failure cases and per-example diffs.
[03:08] Maya: Does this include KV cache correctness checks? We've seen cache drift when quantizing keys in some open-source stacks.
[03:14] Samir: We run KV-stability tests; however some early quant pipelines can cause small numerical drift so we include synthetic prefix tests. If drift exceeds tolerance you get automatic fallback to FP16 for that layer at runtime.
[03:28] Priya: Talking about fallback, what's the runtime behavior on production if a request triggers fallback? Latency spikes?
[03:33] Samir: We do a graceful fallback: per-request we can route to a compatible variant. Two options: synchronous fallback (same request re-run on FP16 variant) which increases latency but preserves accuracy, or asynchronous degrade (serve lower-quality but fast) depending on your policy. We recommend canarying aggressive profiles with traffic splits 5/95 initially.
[03:55] Liam: Can you show the console where we compare FP8 vs INT8 results?
[03:59] Samir: Sure — pulling up the Profile Compare view. You see a matrix: rows are metrics, columns are profiles. There's a delta column and per-example ribbon. Example: prompt #324, INT8-aggressive produced token hallucination at step 12. FP8-balanced matched baseline 98% tokens.
[04:25] Clara: Note, sometimes the transcript might merge names — we had a prior call where 'KV cache' became 'K V cash' — ignore those typos.
[04:34] Priya: On the security side, does the Optimize export include the exact quantized weights or just the profile? We can't accept model artifacts in some clients.
[04:42] Jordan: The export contains recommendations and per-layer quant params, not model binaries. For Private deployments we support a workflow where we ship a recipe that your ops team applies to your on-prem weights; we don't transfer your model weights unless agreed.
[04:58] Darren: That helps. Also SSO and audit logs — will Optimize changes be auditable?
[05:04] Clara: Yes, Console records profile changes, who deployed them, diff, and can tie to SAML SSO user IDs. We retain audit logs per your retention settings (enterprise add-on).
[05:12] Liam: Back to latency — do you have p50/p95 numbers for INT8 vs FP8 for a 2k sequence run?
[05:18] Samir: Quick numbers from our sheet on A100-80gb: baseline FP16 p50: 120ms, p95: 420ms. FP8-balanced p50: 95ms (-21%), p95: 360ms (-14%). INT8-aggressive p50: 70ms (-42%), p95: 320ms (-24%). But note these come with higher variance in quality.
[05:43] Maya: What about memory and batch size? INT8 lets you run larger batch but may hurt tail latency due to batching heuristics.
[05:52] Samir: Right. INT8 reduces GPU memory so you can increase batch size; Optimize recommends batch/queue settings by workload. For ultra-low tail latency we prefer small batch sizes and FP8-balanced usually hits the sweet spot.
[06:06] Liam: Can we run a pilot on our top-100 queries first? We want to see actual MAP.
[06:11] Clara: Absolutely. Typical pilot: you give 1k prompts, we run three profiles (FP16 baseline, FP8-balanced, INT8-aggressive) in the Optimize harness, return per-example diffs and a cost projection.
[06:22] Priya: How long does that run take?
[06:25] Samir: For 1k prompts on A100 it’s ~2–3 hours depending on seq length. Could be faster if we parallelize.
[06:32] Darren: Ok. Also, what's the integration path for our VPC Private deployment? We need to ensure KMS usage for key wrapping of cached tokens.
[06:41] Jordan: For Private we provide a control plane where Optimize recommendations are visible; the actual profile application occurs in your cluster via an agent that applies quantization recipes and reports telemetry — keys remain in your KMS.
[06:53] Liam: Any gotchas we should know? For example, does tokenizer behaviour change with quantization?
[06:58] Samir: Tokenizers unchanged. But model output distribution can shift slightly, causing ranker thresholds to need small adjustments. We usually recommend a short calibration pass.
[07:10] Clara: Let's do a short live demo of an example prompt. Samir, run prompt 'Top product picks for athletic shoes' across three profiles.
[07:18] Samir: Running... [07:26] (typing noises) Results: baseline FP16: ranking A,B,C. FP8-balanced: A,B,C but score deltas small. INT8-aggressive: A,C,B and slight hallucinated attribute for C. See per-example diff.
[07:45] Liam: That's the pattern we feared — ordering swap in INT8. Ok.
[07:50] Priya: If we pin FP8 for re-rank route and INT8 for lower-stakes routes, how do we configure that in infra as code?
[07:58] Jordan: We generate a YAML route config you can commit; it maps route -> profile. API also supports programmatic updates. We recommend a canary rollout CR with traffic split and automated rollback on metric regression.
[08:14] Maya: Can Optimize measure semantic drift or only token-level diffs?
[08:19] Samir: Both. You can plug in your embedding-based similarity metric (Cosine on our embedding API) to detect semantic drift even if token overlap is decent.
[08:30] Darren: Are there hard limits on where FP8 isn't safe? For example, very deep transformer stacks?
[08:36] Samir: Some model architectures with fused attention or custom kernels need special handling; Optimize flags layers where per-layer quant leads to instability and recommends mixed-precision fallback for those layers.
[08:50] Liam: How is model versioning handled? If we pin a model plus profile, can we roll model version and keep profile compatibility?
[08:57] Jordan: Profiles are versioned and tied to model checkpoints by checksum. If a model update breaks a profile we mark it incompatible and you'll see that in Console with suggested re-quantization steps.
[09:10] Priya: On the billing side — what's the delta in inference cost for FP8 vs INT8? We have to model monthly spend.
[09:16] Samir: Rough rule: INT8 can reduce per-token compute cost 30–50% due to smaller kernels and higher throughput. FP8 often gives 15–30% reduction. We'll give a projection based on your QPS and sequence distribution.
[09:28] Liam: Can we try 24-hour soak with a 10% traffic weight? Want to capture rare edge cases.
[09:33] Clara: Yes. Optimize supports scheduled rollouts and time-windowed traffic policies. We'll set up monitoring hooks for your own trace IDs.
[09:42] (02:00) [Note: transcript timestamps after this point are approximate, pace of conversation increased]
[10:00] Samir: I'm going to show the Analyze tab where we run per-example diffs. You can sort by metric delta and inspect tokens with coloured heatmaps — red tokens signal divergence from baseline.
[11:15] Maya: Could we feed back false-positive examples to automatically refine quant profiles?
[11:20] Jordan: We're piloting an adaptive loop where labeled failure cases can nudge recommendations. It's not automatic yet but planned as an Optimize feature.
[11:32] Liam: Curious — do you offer a hybrid where we run FP8 in peak business hours and INT8 overnight for batch jobs?
[11:40] Samir: Yes, routing policies can be time-based. You might choose FP8 for storefront peak and INT8 for offline re-rank jobs.
[11:49] Priya: For Private deployment: is Optimize agent open-source or closed? We need to vet code.
[11:55] Jordan: The agent is provided under enterprise license; we publish an audit package and can do a source review under an NDA.
[12:05] Liam: Anything in compliance we should be cautious about? Logging PII into diffs?
[12:10] Clara: Optimize scrubbers can mask PII in eval sets; for enterprise we do not store raw prompts unless explicitly authorized. Audit log metadata is retained, but payload retention can be disabled.
[12:20] Darren: Great. Let's talk schedule and deliverables.
[12:24] Clara: Proposed pilot plan: (1) NovaRetail supplies 1k prompts + metrics by 2025-04-13, (2) Redwood runs three-profile benchmark and returns report by 2025-04-16, (3) joint review and rollout plan week of 4/21. Sound good?
[12:40] Priya: Yes. We need the security checklist too.
[12:43] Jordan: We'll attach Private deployment checklist and SSO/audit guide.
[12:47] Samir: I'll include micro-benchmarks showing p50/p95 and memory usage per profile on A100 and T4 so you can extrapolate.
[12:55] (Some crosstalk)
[13:05] Clara: Quick Q/A lightning round.
[13:08] Liam: If we see a particular prompt fail on INT8, is there an easy way to tag it to always route to FP16?
[13:14] Samir: Yes — you can set conditional routing rules in the Console: if prompt matches regex or if classifier predicts high-risk, route to FP16. We can demo that in the next call.
[13:26] Maya: How do you handle third-party model variants? We use a community model fork sometimes.
[13:30] Jordan: We support customer-supplied checkpoints for Private deployments; Optimize will attempt quantization but may flag incompatibilities.
[13:38] Liam: Any competitor pitfalls we should watch for?
[13:41] Clara: Some competitors require shipping model binaries, others lack per-route policies or per-example diffs. We can share a competitive matrix after.
[13:52] Priya: Ok, let's confirm next steps.
[13:55] Clara: Recap: Redwood to run micro-benchmarks and share spreadsheets, NovaRetail to send 1k prompts by 4/13, schedule follow-up week of 4/16. Clara to send pricing delta and SOW. Jordan to send security checklist and agent audit package. Samir to run A100/T4 profile runs and include memory/batch guidance.
[14:20] Darren: That works. Any blockers?
[14:24] Liam: None from ML side. Priya might have infra calendar conflicts but we'll let you know.
[14:29] Clara: Great. We'll email the calendar invite for follow-up. Thanks all.
[14:35] (Call ends)
